author: Theophilus of Alexandria
occasion: The surviving fragment comments on a passage marked as John 3. The author uses the verse to refute a doctrine he regards as unlawful, namely that souls are sent from heaven into bodies for punishment.
argument: Theophilus argues that Christ overturned an unlawful doctrine held by some who supposed that sinning souls are sent from heaven into bodies for punishment. According to this error, the soul sometimes pre-exists the body by itself, and sometimes is joined to bodies on account of its own sins, so that a woman can conceive only when some soul sins. Christ, when asked, destroys this error by saying that neither this one nor his parents sinned, but that the works of God might be revealed.

outline.move: The fragment explains that Christ overturned an unlawful doctrine about souls being sent into bodies for punishment, and quotes his answer from the passage marked as John 3.

key_terms.sense: An unlawful or lawless teaching, specifically the belief that souls are sent into bodies as punishment for sins.
The soul, understood by the opponents as pre-existing the body and being joined to it because of sin.
Pre-existing, referring to the soul existing before the body.
Punishment, the reason the opponents think souls are sent from heaven into bodies.
Error or deception, the false belief Christ destroys.
The works of God, the purpose for which the condition occurred according to Christ.
